source.title: Large Language Models as Foundations for Next-Gen Dense Retrieval: A Comprehensive Empirical Assessment
source.authors: Kun Luo; Ming-Hao Qin; Zheng Liu; Shi-Tao Xiao; Jun Zhao; Kang Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream dense-retrieval performance across backbone models of different sizes and configurations, extending scale-related questions to retrieval. It does not measure pretraining cross-entropy loss or compute-optimal training allocations.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law work but does not report those cited results as its own. Its outcomes are retrieval scores, not held-out language-model loss. Rows below cover reported model-level aggregate scores in Tables 3–6; detailed per-task scores in Tables 3, 4 and 6, data-efficiency results in Table 1/Figure 2, and detailed length results in Table 7/Figure 3 are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes over 15 backbones (0.1B–32B) for dense retrieval and reports downstream retrieval scores by model size and pretraining amount. These results bear on whether downstream performance improves with scale (V6) in a new setting. It fits no scaling law and measures no pretraining loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude that larger size and more pretraining both raise in-domain accuracy and data efficiency. Size is the main driver of zero-shot, long-input and multi-task gains. Instruction training helps LLM retrievers but not BERT, and chat alignment adds nothing over base models.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes backbone encoders for dense retrieval and evaluates retrieval metrics across models and settings; it does not fit language-model loss scaling laws or allocate pretraining compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with model family and pretraining sufficiency, chat alignment, instruction training, retrieval task, and single-task versus multi-task training.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, 2024
record.problems: The paper compares models that differ in architecture, pretraining amount and other configurations, so parameter-count effects are not cleanly isolated. It reports no uncertainty estimates for the listed scores and does not fit or validate a predictive scaling law.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1/Figure 2 data-efficiency step comparisons; per-task results in Tables 3, 4 and 6; and the detailed passage-length sweep in Table 7/Figure 3 were not extracted. The selected rows retain model-level aggregate measures and comparisons relevant to downstream retrieval performance across scale.

untested.parts: Predictability: no fitted law of downstream score against parameters, tokens or loss, and no extrapolation. Pretraining loss is never measured. Size is not varied under controlled pretraining except within Qwen1.5.

missing.what: Data efficiency: after 100 steps Llama-2-7B scores 39.0 vs Qwen-0.5B 33.6 vs BERT-large 24.6 (NDCG@10). Larger models also have a smaller gap to full training.
Lengthy retrieval on NarrativeQA (256–8192 tokens): Qwen1.5 0.5B→4B→7B→32B rises at each length. Llama3-8B leads at 256/512. Columns for BERT appear misaligned in the extracted text.
Unseen-instruction robustness: MSMARCO-OOD rises with size, 39.3 (BERT-large) → 43.6 → 47.0 → 48.9 (Qwen-14B), 49.6 (Llama-3-8B).

record.verdict_notes: All rows were marked 'partial' by the reader. Within-family size trends are actually clean and monotonic, so those rows are 'observed'. Size confounds appear only across families, where pretraining token count differs. The study supports 'downstream improves with scale' qualitatively, after task fine-tuning. It says nothing about predictability or a fitted form. Kaplan et al. is only cited as background.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from small-run fits.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation trends.
Architecture effects at a fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss in other modalities or training regimes.
The study measures downstream dense-retrieval scores, not language-model loss; it does not test a fitted predictive law or downstream tasks outside dense retrieval.
Fitted exponents, fitting choices, and departures from power-law curves.

relationships.condition: Within a model family (Qwen1.5 base and chat, BERT, T5), across in-domain MS MARCO, BEIR zero-shot, instruction-based and multi-task retrieval
relationships.reason: Scores rise monotonically with size in every within-family series (r1–r5, r13–r19, r21–r23, r31–r34, r36–r38, r40–r42, r44–r47).
relationships.display_finding: Retrieval scores increased monotonically with size in every tested within-family series across in-domain, zero-shot, instruction-based, and multitask settings.

relationships.condition: Across model families for in-domain MS MARCO accuracy, where pretraining amount differs
relationships.reason: Parameter count alone does not order in-domain scores. Qwen-0.5B (36.7) beats Phi-1.5-1.3B (34.1), Gemma-2B beats T5-xxl, and Llama-3-8B equals Llama-2-13B. Authors attribute this to pretraining tokens (r6–r13).
relationships.display_finding: Qwen-0.5B scored 36.7 versus 34.1 for Phi-1.5-1.3B, Gemma-2B beat T5-xxl, and Llama-3-8B matched Llama-2-13B, which the authors linked to pretraining-token differences.

relationships.condition: Across families on BEIR zero-shot and instruction retrieval
relationships.reason: Size mostly orders scores, with small inversions: Llama-3-8B 50.4 < Gemma-7B 51.2, and Llama-3-8B ≈ Qwen-14B under instructions (r24–r30, r39).
relationships.display_finding: Size mostly ordered performance, but Llama-3-8B scored 50.4 versus 51.2 for Gemma-7B and approximately matched Qwen-14B under instruction retrieval.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported model-size comparisons for MS MARCO in-domain retrieval, BEIR average retrieval, and the reported instruction/multi-task task averages
reader_labels.reason: Scores generally rise across the reported size comparisons; for example, the Qwen1.5 series increases in the reported MS MARCO and BEIR averages (r13–r16, r31–r34). These are retrieval outcomes, not fitted predictive laws.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Comparisons across model families and alignment/training settings
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that pretraining sufficiency, architecture, and alignment also matter, and some smaller models outperform larger ones; the comparisons do not isolate parameter count or establish a stable prediction rule (r6–r12, r21–r30, r35–r43).
